topic: Writing piecewise rules for rates and fees
subtitle: Writing the rule from a price list, using it to find a charge, and working back from a charge

problems.desc: Part (a): the rule must have two branches with their conditions attached -- 3 plus 2 times m dollars when m is at most 5 miles, and 13 plus 1.5 times the quantity m minus 5 when m is more than 5 miles. Full credit requires the SECOND branch to start from the 13 dollars already charged at 5 miles and to charge the lower rate only on the miles beyond 5; a second branch written as 1.5 times m is the common error and is not full credit.

Part (a): the rule must be 5 dollars when the stay t is at most 2 hours, and 5 plus 3 times the quantity t minus 2 when t is more than 2 hours. Full credit requires the flat first branch (no t in it at all) and the subtraction of 2 in the second branch, so that the extra charge starts from the third hour rather than from the first.

Part (a): the rule must be 25 dollars when the data used g is at most 5 gigabytes, and 25 plus 10 times the quantity g minus 5 when g is more than 5. Full credit requires the condition on each branch to be written down, not just the two formulas, and the second branch must charge the extra 10 dollars per gigabyte only beyond the fifth.

problems.slot: (b) why the second branch was used
problems.desc: Part (b): a correct answer must say that a fare of 25 dollars is larger than the 13 dollars charged at exactly 5 miles, so the ride must be longer than 5 miles and therefore lands in the second branch. It must also confirm afterwards that the answer really does satisfy that condition. Guessing the branch without comparing 25 to the 13-dollar boundary value is not full credit.

Part (a): the rule must be 0 dollars when the number of days d is at most 3, and 0.25 times the quantity d minus 3 when d is more than 3. Full credit requires the subtraction of 3, so that day 4 costs 25 cents rather than a dollar, and requires the first branch to be exactly zero.

Part (a): the rule must be 18 times h when the hours h are at most 40, and 720 plus 27 times the quantity h minus 40 when h is more than 40. Full credit requires the 720 (which is 18 times 40, the pay already earned at the boundary) and the higher rate 27 applied only to the hours past 40. Writing the second branch as 27 times h is the classic error and is not full credit.

problems.slot: (b) why the overtime branch was used
problems.desc: Part (b): a correct answer must say that 963 dollars is more than the 720 dollars a full 40-hour week pays, so the week must have run past 40 hours and the overtime branch applies. Checking the answer against the condition at the end is part of full credit; picking the branch by trial is not.

problems.slot: (a) the piecewise rule for plan B
problems.desc: Part (a): the rule must be 20 dollars when the minutes n are at most 200, and 20 plus 0.15 times the quantity n minus 200 when n is more than 200. Full credit requires both conditions and the subtraction of 200 in the second branch.

problems.slot: (c) which plan is cheaper below that point
problems.desc: Part (c): a correct answer must say that plan B is cheaper for every number of minutes below the break-even value and more expensive above it, and must support that with evidence -- either a test value on each side, or the observation that B rises 0.15 dollars per minute past 200 while A rises only 0.10, so B eventually overtakes A. A bare assertion with no test value and no rate comparison is not full credit.
